objectives: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of tRNS in various psychiatric disorders.
inclusion_criteria: This review focused on people who were diagnosed with a psychiatric illness and were being treated using tRNS. Since tRNS is a relatively newer neuromodulation technique, with fewer articles available on the subject matter, articles of quantitative, qualitative or mixed-method designs, case studies or series were all included. These articles focused on the safety, efficacy and clinical applicability of tRNS in the management of psychiatric disorders. Only peer reviewed articles published in the English language were selected.
exclusion_criteria: All studies that dealt with medical illnesses with no comorbid psychiatric disorders were excluded. The review also excluded papers that used tRNS on non-psychiatric populations or healthy controls. Studies focusing only on any other neuromodulation techniques like tDCS or tACS, without using tRNS as an intervention strategy, were also excluded. Lastly, opinion pieces, editorials, or letters without primary data were also excluded.
pmid_query: A total of four databases were searched for the selection of studies in this review. This included CENTRAL-Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Additional articles were identified by cross referencing the selected articles from these databases. Studies were included from their inception to 30th April, 2025. Boolean operators along with database specific index terms were used to refine the search strategy.
selection_evidence: Results/PRISMA report 22 included studies (278 records identified, 138 duplicates removed, 104 excluded at title/abstract screening, and 14 more excluded as abstracts, a conference paper, or ongoing trial-registry records). Table 1 contains 22 included-study rows. Table 2 confirms 16 randomized controlled trials ([11],[26],[27],[12],[14],[13],[17],[31],[28],[16],[22],[20],[29],[21],[25],[9]); Table 3 adds 2 experimental studies ([10],[18]); the remaining 4 case/case-series studies are Chan [15], Palm [19], Haesebaert [23], and Mondino [24]. Cross-checking the reference list shows ref 30 (McGough et al., trigeminal nerve stimulation) is cited only in discussion and is not an included tRNS study, leaving 22 included references in total.
notes: Table 1 OCR appears to misread Murphy et al. 2023 as [29] and Yeh et al. 2022b as [27]; Table 2 and the reference list correct these to [31] and [29]. The manuscript did not provide a literal Boolean search string, so the pmid_query field uses the most explicit search-strategy wording available from the main/supplemental text.
pmid_query_exact_source: ("transcranial random noise stimulation" OR "tRNS") AND ("psychiatric disorder" OR "psychiatric disorders" OR "mental disorder" OR "mental disorders" OR depression OR schizophrenia OR anxiety OR ADHD OR dyslexia OR "attention deficit")
pmid_query_repair_notes: Original pmid_query was a database-search description with no exact PubMed string. No exact query was recoverable from main_text.txt or supplementary files. Query constructed from paper scope: tRNS interventions across psychiatric disorders (ADHD, dyslexia, schizophrenia, depression, anxiety) as described in Abstract and Results. Searched CENTRAL, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science from inception to April 30, 2025.
